status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Spot-checked this Ethiopian translation's own extracted text across chapters 1-16 and the closing verses of chapter 21 against the KJV verse-for-verse (wording, verse numbering, and pericope boundaries all match exactly, including the disputed pericopes) - this book is textually identical to KJV John in this translation, so the KJV Character Index's tier structure and character roster is reused wholesale (adapted, not re-derived from scratch), with every id re-suffixed "_ethiopian_john" to keep it scoped separately from the KJV set per the schema's collision-avoidance rule. All naming-collision flags carried over unchanged since they are properties of the text itself, not the translation: John the Baptist vs. the traditional (never textually asserted) identification of the unnamed "beloved disciple" with John the son of Zebedee; three distinct women named Mary (mother of Jesus, Magdalene, of Bethany) plus a fourth mentioned once and left unindexed (wife of Cleophas, 19:25); Judas Iscariot vs. "Judas, not Iscariot" (14:22); Simon Peter vs. Simon the father of Judas Iscariot (6:71). The two adversarial-review promotions from the KJV pass (Philip and Joseph of Arimathea each getting their own full manager tier rather than sitting as submanagers) are preserved here since they rest on the same textual actions, confirmed present verbatim in this translation (Philip called directly at 1:43, tested at 6:5-7, brings the Greeks at 12:20-22, presses Jesus at 14:8-9; Joseph independently secures Pilate's permission at 19:38 before Nicodemus joins at 19:39). The textually disputed pericope of the woman taken in adultery (7:53-8:11) and the "angel troubled the water" clause (5:4) are both present in this Ethiopian text exactly as in KJV, indexed as-is per the project's guiding principle of never editing scripture, with the same factual (not doctrinal) manuscript-history caveat. No content differences from KJV were found anywhere in this book - unlike this Bible's own Ezra (which follows the 1 Esdras tradition), John here is a straightforward shared-canon match.

scribeTiers.scribeName: The Ruler Who Came By Night

characters.name: Jesus Christ

genealogy.father: joseph — referenced only by others as Jesus's father (John 1:45, 6:42), not narrated as a character in this book

verses.note: Prologue: 'In the beginning was the Word'; 'the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.'
Turns water to wine at a wedding in Cana — 'the beginning of miracles.'
Cleanses the temple; 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.'
Reveals himself as Messiah directly to the Samaritan woman.
Heals the Capernaum nobleman's son from a distance with a word.
Heals a man infirm 38 years at the pool of Bethesda.
Feeds five thousand with five loaves and two small fishes.
Walks on the sea to the disciples' ship.
'Before Abraham was, I am.'
Raises Lazarus from the dead, the last and greatest of the seven signs.
Triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
Washes the disciples' feet at supper.
Betrayed, arrested in the garden, and tried before Annas, Caiaphas, and Pilate.
Crucified; 'I thirst'; 'It is finished.'
Appears to the disciples in a locked room; breathes on them, 'Receive ye the Holy Ghost.'
Appears at the Sea of Tiberias, directs the great catch of fish.

funFacts: John's Gospel organizes its first half around seven distinct miraculous 'signs' rather than a broad chronicle of miracles as in the Synoptics.
Unlike Matthew or Luke, John gives no birth narrative — the book opens instead with a theological prologue identifying Jesus as 'the Word.'

characters.name: John the Baptist

verses.note: Introduced as 'a man sent from God' to bear witness of the Light.
Denies being the Christ, Elias, or 'that prophet'; identifies himself as 'the voice of one crying in the wilderness.'
'Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.'
Testifies he saw the Spirit descend like a dove and rest on Jesus.
Two of his own disciples leave him to follow Jesus at his word.
Further testimony to his own disciples: 'He must increase, but I must decrease.'

funFacts: John's Gospel never actually narrates John baptizing Jesus, nor does it call him 'the Baptist' at all — that title is a Synoptic convention; here he is simply 'John.'

characters.name: Simon Peter

genealogy.father: Jona/Jonas — John 1:42 ('Simon the son of Jona'), John 21:15-17 ('Simon, son of Jonas') — not itself a tracked character

verses.note: Brought to Jesus by his brother Andrew; Jesus renames him 'Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.'
When many disciples turn back, Peter answers, 'Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.'
Protests Jesus washing his feet, then asks for hands and head as well.
Vows to lay down his life for Jesus; Jesus predicts his three denials before the cock crows.
Draws his sword in Gethsemane and cuts off the right ear of Malchus, the high priest's servant.
Denies Jesus three times in the high priest's courtyard.
Runs to the empty tomb with the beloved disciple; enters and sees the linen clothes.
Girds his coat and casts himself into the sea on hearing 'It is the Lord.'
Threefold restoration: 'Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?' — 'Feed my sheep.'
Jesus foretells the manner of Peter's death.

funFacts: John's account of the arrest omits Simon of Cyrene entirely — unlike the Synoptics, John states Jesus bore his own cross (19:17).

characters.name: Andrew

genealogy.father: Jona/Jonas — John 1:42, not itself a tracked character

verses.note: One of John the Baptist's two disciples who follows Jesus first; finds his brother Simon and brings him to Jesus.
Points out the lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes before the feeding of the 5,000.
With Philip, brings word to Jesus that certain Greeks wish to see him.

funFacts: Explicitly named 'Simon Peter's brother' (John 1:40).

verses.note: Servant of the high priest; Peter cuts off his right ear with a sword in Gethsemane.
A kinsman of Malchus, present at Peter's third denial, asks if he saw Peter in the garden with Jesus.

characters.name: Philip

verses.note: Called directly by Jesus, 'of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter'; finds Nathanael, 'Come and see.'
Jesus tests him about feeding the crowd; Philip estimates 200 pennyworth of bread wouldn't suffice.
Approached by the Greeks seeking Jesus; tells Andrew, and together they tell Jesus.
'Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us'; Jesus answers, 'he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.'

funFacts: Called directly by Jesus ('Follow me,' 1:43) rather than being brought by another disciple.

characters.name: Nathanael

verses.note: Told by Philip, 'We have found him... Jesus of Nazareth'; skeptical of Nazareth, but Jesus calls him 'an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.'
Amazed Jesus saw him 'under the fig tree'; confesses, 'thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.'
Listed 'of Cana in Galilee' among the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias.

funFacts: Traditionally identified with the apostle Bartholomew, but 'Bartholomew' never appears anywhere in John's Gospel.

characters.name: Nicodemus
characters.scribeTier: The Ruler Who Came By Night

verses.note: 'A ruler of the Jews' and Pharisee, comes to Jesus by night: 'we know that thou art a teacher come from God.'
Questions how a man can be 'born again'; Jesus answers, 'Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things?'
Defends Jesus's right to a hearing before the chief priests and Pharisees.
Brings about a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes and joins Joseph of Arimathea to wrap and bury Jesus's body.

funFacts: Appears at three separate, spaced-out points across the whole book.
Joins Joseph of Arimathea for the burial itself, but it is Joseph who independently secures Pilate's legal permission beforehand (19:38).

characters.name: The Samaritan Woman

spouses: a sixth man she was living with who was 'not her husband' — John 4:18

verses.note: Comes to Jacob's well to draw water; Jesus asks her for a drink.
Asks for the living water Jesus describes; Jesus reveals knowledge of her five husbands and current situation.
Calls him a prophet and raises the dispute over the proper place of worship.
Speaks of the coming Messiah; Jesus tells her plainly, 'I that speak unto thee am he.'
Leaves her waterpot, testifies in the city, and many Samaritans believe on Jesus through her word.

funFacts: Never named in the text; left unnamed per this project's rule against assigning names not given in scripture itself.

characters.name: The Nobleman of Capernaum

children: unnamed son, healed by Jesus's word — John 4:46-54, not individually indexed

verses.note: A 'nobleman' of Capernaum comes to Jesus in Cana and besought him to heal his son, who lay at the point of death.
Jesus answers, 'Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe.'
The nobleman pleads again; Jesus says, 'Go thy way; thy son liveth,' and the man believed.
His servants meet him on the road with news the son was healed at the very hour Jesus spoke.

funFacts: The second of John's seven signs.
Not named in the text; 'nobleman' renders a Greek term for a royal official.

characters.name: The Impotent Man at Bethesda

verses.note: Lies among 'a great multitude of impotent folk' at the pool of Bethesda, having had an infirmity thirty and eight years.
Jesus asks, 'Wilt thou be made whole?'; the man answers he has 'no man' to put him into the pool.
Jesus says, 'Rise, take up thy bed, and walk'; he is immediately made whole.
Questioned by the Jews for carrying his bed on the sabbath; does not yet know who healed him.
Jesus finds him afterward in the temple: 'sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.'
Goes and tells the Jews it was Jesus who made him whole.

funFacts: The third of John's seven signs.

The clause describing an angel troubling the water (John 5:4) is textually disputed, present in this translation exactly as in the KJV — indexed as-is per this project's guiding principle of never editing scripture.

characters.name: The Man Born Blind

verses.note: Blind from birth; Jesus anoints his eyes with clay and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam, and he receives sight.
Neighbors question whether he is really the same man who used to beg.
Brought to the Pharisees; his healing causes division over whether Jesus is from God.
'One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.'
Argues boldly with the Pharisees that a man could do nothing 'except he were of God.'
Cast out of the synagogue for his testimony.
Jesus finds him, reveals himself as the Son of God; the man worships him, 'Lord, I believe.'

funFacts: Alone among the Gospels' healing accounts, John 9 gives the healed man an extended, first-person cross-examination scene before the religious authorities.
His parents are mentioned but left unnamed by the text itself, afraid to answer plainly 'for fear of the Jews' (9:22-23).

characters.name: Lazarus of Bethany

verses.note: Falls sick in Bethany; his sisters send word to Jesus, 'he whom thou lovest is sick.'
Jesus tells the disciples plainly, 'Lazarus is dead.'
Raised after four days in the tomb: 'Lazarus, come forth'; comes out still bound in graveclothes.
Sits at supper with Jesus in Bethany six days before the Passover.
The chief priests plot to kill him too, since many Jews believed on Jesus because of him.

funFacts: Brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany (John 11:1).
'Jesus wept' (John 11:35) is the shortest verse in the KJV; identical wording appears in this translation.

characters.name: Martha of Bethany

verses.note: Goes out to meet Jesus on the road while Mary stays in the house.
'Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.'
Affirms belief in the resurrection 'at the last day'; confesses, 'I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God.'
Raises the practical objection at the tomb: 'Lord, by this time he stinketh.'
Serves at the supper given for Jesus in Bethany.

funFacts: Sister of Lazarus and Mary of Bethany.

characters.name: Mary of Bethany

verses.note: Introduced by the narrator as 'that Mary which anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair.'
Falls at Jesus's feet weeping, repeating Martha's words.
Anoints Jesus's feet with a pound of costly spikenard ointment and wipes them with her hair.

funFacts: Sister of Lazarus and Martha; a distinct woman from Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Jesus.

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathea

verses.note: 'A disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews,' besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate gave him leave.
Nicodemus joins him, bringing about a hundred pound weight of myrrh and aloes.
Together they wind Jesus's body in linen clothes with the spices and lay it in a new sepulchre.

funFacts: Acts alone in securing Pilate's legal permission before Nicodemus joins him for the burial itself.
John's Gospel identifies him only as 'a disciple... secretly for fear of the Jews,' unlike the Synoptics' fuller detail.

characters.name: Thomas

verses.note: When Jesus resolves to go to Lazarus despite danger, Thomas says, 'Let us also go, that we may die with him.'
'Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?'
Absent at Jesus's first resurrection appearance; declares he will not believe without seeing and touching the print of the nails.
Eight days later, Jesus invites him to touch his hands and side; Thomas answers, 'My Lord and my God.'
Jesus: 'blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.'
Present with the other disciples at the Sea of Tiberias.

funFacts: 'Didymus' is Greek for 'twin'; the text never identifies or names his twin.
The source of the popular nickname 'doubting Thomas.'

genealogy.father: Simon — John 6:71, 13:26 ('Judas Iscariot, Simon's son'), distinct from Simon Peter, not itself a tracked character

verses.note: Jesus says 'one of you is a devil,' identifying Judas as his future betrayer.
Objects to Mary's costly ointment; the text notes he 'had the bag, and bare what was put therein,' calling him a thief.
'The devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot... to betray him.'
Receives the sop from Jesus at supper; 'Satan entered into him.'
Goes out immediately into the night.
Leads a band of men and officers to arrest Jesus in a garden he knew well.

characters.name: Caiaphas

verses.note: As high priest that year, prophesies (unwittingly, per the narrator) 'that one man should die for the people.'
Jesus is brought to him after Annas.
Annas sends Jesus, still bound, on to Caiaphas.
Jesus is led from Caiaphas's house to the Roman hall of judgment.

funFacts: Son-in-law of Annas (John 18:13).

verses.note: Jesus is brought to him first, 'father in law to Caiaphas.'
Questions Jesus about his doctrine and disciples; an officer strikes Jesus for his answer.
Sends Jesus bound on to Caiaphas.

characters.name: The Pharisees and Chief Priests

verses.note: Send officers to take Jesus; the officers return without him, 'Never man spake like this man.'
Council convened over Jesus and Lazarus; they take counsel to put Jesus to death.
Furnish the band of men and officers who go with Judas to arrest Jesus.
Cry out 'Crucify him, crucify him' before Pilate.

funFacts: Treated as a single collective entry since the text does not differentiate individual Pharisees or chief priests in these group scenes.

characters.name: Pontius Pilate

verses.note: The Jews bring Jesus to him but will not enter the judgment hall themselves.
Questions Jesus, 'Art thou the King of the Jews?'; Pilate asks, 'What is truth?'
Offers to release Jesus per the Passover custom; the crowd chooses Barabbas instead.
Has Jesus scourged and mocked with a crown of thorns; presents him, 'Behold the man!'
Asks Jesus, 'Whence art thou?'; Jesus tells him his power is 'given thee from above.'
Pressured by the cry 'thou art not Caesar's friend'; delivers Jesus to be crucified.
Writes the title 'JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS' and refuses to alter the wording.
Grants Joseph of Arimathea permission to take Jesus's body.

funFacts: John is the only Gospel that records Pilate's question 'What is truth?' (18:38).
John's account of Pilate's court does not include the hand-washing scene found in Matthew's Gospel.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene

verses.note: Stands by the cross of Jesus alongside his mother and Mary the wife of Cleophas.
Comes early to the tomb, finds the stone taken away, and runs to tell Peter and 'the other disciple, whom Jesus loved.'
Weeps at the tomb, sees two angels, then Jesus himself (mistaking him for the gardener) until he calls her by name, 'Mary' — 'Rabboni.'
Told 'Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended'; goes and tells the disciples, 'I have seen the Lord.'

funFacts: Named for Magdala; the 'seven devils' detail associated with her elsewhere comes from Luke/Mark, not from John's own text.

characters.name: The Disciple Whom Jesus Loved

verses.note: Leans on Jesus's breast at supper and asks, at Peter's prompting, who the betrayer is.
From the cross, Jesus entrusts his mother's care to this disciple: 'Behold thy mother!'
Outruns Peter to the empty tomb, looks in, and 'saw, and believed.'
Recognizes the risen Jesus on the shore first: 'It is the Lord.'
A rumor that he would not die is corrected by the narrator; identified as the disciple who 'testifieth of these things, and wrote these things.'

funFacts: Never named directly anywhere in the text. Church tradition identifies him with John the son of Zebedee, but this book's own text never makes that identification explicitly.

An unnamed 'other disciple, known unto the high priest' who brings Peter into the courtyard during the trial (18:15-16) is popularly assumed to be this same disciple, but the text itself does not say so.

spouses: joseph — referenced only by others regarding Jesus's parentage (John 1:45, 6:42), not narrated as a character in this book

verses.note: At the wedding in Cana, tells Jesus 'They have no wine,' then instructs the servants, 'Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.'
Stands by the cross; Jesus entrusts her care to the beloved disciple, who 'took her unto his own home.'

characters.name: The Woman Taken in Adultery

verses.note: Scribes and Pharisees bring her to Jesus, testing him about the law of Moses regarding adultery.
Jesus answers, 'He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.'
Her accusers depart one by one; Jesus tells her, 'Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.'

funFacts: This passage (John 7:53-8:11) is noted by many textual scholars as absent from the earliest surviving manuscripts of John; it is indexed here exactly as it stands in this translation's own text, unaltered, per this project's guiding principle of never editing scripture.

characters.name: The Bread of Life Discourse
characters.purpose: Following the feeding of the five thousand, Jesus reinterprets the sign as teaching about himself as the true, life-giving bread come down from heaven, sifting the crowd's and even his own disciples' commitment to him.

verses.note: Rebukes the crowd for seeking him only because they ate of the loaves.
'I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger.'
Describes himself as 'the living bread which came down from heaven.'
The 'hard saying' about eating his flesh and drinking his blood.
Many of his disciples find the teaching too hard and 'walked no more with him.'
Asks the Twelve if they will also leave; Peter answers, 'Lord, to whom shall we go?'

characters.name: The Good Shepherd Discourse
characters.purpose: Jesus describes his relationship to his followers through shepherd imagery — knowing his sheep, laying down his life for them willingly, and gathering 'other sheep' beyond the immediate fold — teaching that provokes a charge of blasphemy from his hearers.

verses.note: Parable of the sheepfold and the shepherd who enters by the door.
'I am the door of the sheep' / 'I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.'
'I know my sheep, and am known of mine... other sheep I have, which are not of this fold.'
'My sheep hear my voice... I and my Father are one.'
The Jews take up stones, charging him with blasphemy for making himself God.

characters.name: The Upper Room Discourse
characters.purpose: On the night before his crucifixion, Jesus prepares his disciples for his departure: comforting them, promising the coming of the Holy Spirit, describing their ongoing relationship to him through the vine-and-branches image, commanding them to love one another, and warning them of the world's coming hatred.

verses.note: 'Let not your heart be troubled... In my Father's house are many mansions.'
'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.'
Promises 'another Comforter,' the Holy Ghost, who will teach and bring all things to remembrance.
'Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.'
'I am the true vine... without me ye can do nothing.'
'This is my commandment, That ye love one another... Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.'
Warns that the world will hate them as it hated him.
Describes the coming work of the Comforter, to guide them 'into all truth.'
'In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.'

characters.name: The High Priestly Prayer
characters.purpose: On the eve of his arrest, Jesus prays aloud in the hearing of his disciples — for himself, for his immediate followers, and for all who would later believe through their word — a prayer for unity, protection, and sanctification rather than a teaching addressed to people directly.

verses.note: 'Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son.'
Prays the Father would 'keep through thine own name' the disciples he leaves behind.
'I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.'
'Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.'
Extends the prayer to 'them also which shall believe on me through their word,' asking 'that they all may be one.'

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above per the rule against inventing differentiation the text doesn't support.

sons_of_zebedee.note: James and John, sons of Zebedee, listed among seven disciples present at the Sea of Tiberias. Not individually indexed — John's Gospel never names 'James' at all, and while church tradition identifies 'John' with the beloved disciple, the text itself never equates them explicitly.

judas_not_iscariot.note: 'Judas (not Iscariot)' asks Jesus a single question during the Upper Room Discourse. Distinguished by the text itself from Judas Iscariot; not otherwise developed.

mary_wife_of_cleophas.note: One of the women standing by the cross alongside Jesus's mother and Mary Magdalene. A fourth distinct 'Mary' in this book, left unindexed given the single mention.

jesus_brethren.note: Jesus's brethren urge him to go up to the feast in Judaea; the narrator notes 'neither did his brethren believe in him.' Unnamed, not individually indexed.

other_disciple_known_to_high_priest.note: An unnamed disciple 'known unto the high priest' who brings Peter into the courtyard during the trial before Annas. Often popularly assumed to be the beloved disciple, but the text does not explicitly make that identification.

barabbas.note: 'A robber'; the prisoner the crowd chooses to have released instead of Jesus, per the Passover custom. Not otherwise developed.
